original_question:
Write a Verilog module named `adder_4bit`.
The module should have the following interface:
Inputs:
  `[3:0] A`
  `[3:0] B`
  `CIN`
  `CLK`
  `RST`
Outputs:
  `[3:0] SUM`
  `COUT`

The module should implement a registered 4-bit adder with carry-in and a specific carry-out.
On the positive edge of the clock (`CLK`), the output `SUM` should update to the 4-bit result of adding inputs `A`, `B`, and `CIN`.
Simultaneously on the positive edge of `CLK`, the output `COUT` should update to the result of the logic expression `(A[3] & B[3]) | (A[3] & CIN) | (B[3] & CIN)`.
The module must include an asynchronous, active-low reset (`RST`). When `RST` is low, both the `SUM` and `COUT` outputs should be asynchronously cleared to 0.
